clue.text: Argue with son in cantankerous terms

indicators.note: the son is placed inside the phrase made of the other two words

parts.note: cantankerous means cross, bad-tempered
terms are words
S is the standard abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone quarrels with their boy using grumpy language.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is an idiom for having a dispute or clash with someone.

clue.text: Placed Castro in charge of a republic nearby

indicators.note: the letters of Castro are set down in a new arrangement, so placed signals the shuffle

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fidel Castro is put in control of a neighbouring Central American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Placed' rearranges CASTRO into COSTAR. From the surface's Cuba, the Central American country is fairly near.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a Central American republic, not far from the Cuba the surface evokes.

clue.text: Fleet, maybe? The devil it is!

definitions.meaning: the Fleet was a famous London prison, an example of a former jail, nick being British slang for prison
a traditional jocular English nickname for Satan

explanation.definitionFit: The Fleet was a historic prison, a jail of yesteryear in slang terms, and the same phrase is a folksy name for Satan.

clue.text: Covering sorcerer with hessian results in a brawl

indicators.note: in a down answer the fabric sits on top of the magician, covering him

parts.note: scrim is a coarse open-weave fabric like hessian
a mage is a magician or sorcerer

explanation.surface: Throwing sackcloth over a wizard leads to a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrimmage is a confused scuffle or tussle, a variant of skirmish.

clue.text: What's utterly essential for power?

indicators.note: read as 'when uttered', so the word what's is to be spoken and its sound taken

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: A question asking what is absolutely vital for energy supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' looks like an intensifier for 'essential' but means 'when uttered'.
explanation.definitionFit: The watt is the SI unit in which power is measured, so these units are basic to any statement of electrical output.

clue.text: Getting plants firmly established is cheering

definitions.meaning: a plant that is taking hold in soil is growing roots
to root for a team is to cheer it on

explanation.definitionFit: Plants grow roots to settle in, and rooting for someone is supporting them with shouts.

clue.text: Logs I ordered in Ireland

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in Ireland

indicators.note: the letters are put in a different order, so ordered signals the rearrangement

explanation.surface: An Irish customer puts in an order for firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a town and county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Fellow accustomed to being in a union

parts.note: used, as in used to, means accustomed

explanation.surface: A man gets used to married life.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are fused are joined together, melded into one.

clue.text: Initially in favour of automatic ignition

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for
starters are the motors that start an engine automatically

explanation.surface: Someone backs self-starting engines.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to begin with or first of all, a synonym of at the outset.

clue.text: Strangely ignorant about one method of conservation

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the single letter
the word ignorant is to be read in a strange new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An oddly uninformed take on one way of saving the environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' gives RATONING; 'about' wraps it round the I. 'Conservation' suggests wildlife, but here it means saving scarce supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Rationing conserves scarce supplies by limiting each person's share, as in wartime Britain.

clue.text: Chess champ made a terrific teacher

parts.note: grand means terrific, splendid
a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A chess winner turned out to be a superb tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: The top title awarded to elite chess players by the world chess federation.

clue.text: Pragmatic attitude is found in sovereign's domain

indicators.note: the small word is found inside the domain word

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom, the land a monarch rules
taken as written

explanation.surface: Practical thinking prevails in the monarch's kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is a practical, matter-of-fact outlook, accepting things as they are.

clue.text: Trip to Australia with a Dutch sage

parts.note: a spin is a short trip or drive
Oz is informal for Australia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Dutch philosopher takes a holiday down under.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a 17th-century philosopher from Amsterdam, a sage being a wise thinker.

clue.text: Swindle that puts Rex in credit

indicators.note: the king's letter goes into the word for credit

parts.note: on tick is British slang for on credit
R stands for Rex, Latin for king, as on coins

explanation.surface: A fraud involving putting the king in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick is a con or deception, a way of cheating someone.

clue.text: Revoked by a British Opposition leader in confinement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: gated means confined to school or college premises as a punishment

explanation.surface: Something cancelled by a British opposition leader who is under house arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or agreement is to repeal or annul it formally.

clue.text: Hack violinists put it on their bows before

parts.words: violinists put it on their bows
parts.note: rosin is the resin rubbed on violin bows for grip
ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: Violinists prepare their bows before playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' is not a journalist but a worn-out horse: Rosinante is Don Quixote's nag in Cervantes's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is an old riding horse, and Rosinante is the famous broken-down steed of Don Quixote.

clue.text: Difficult assignment for fraternity of high standing

parts.note: tall means of great height, standing high
an order is a brotherhood, as in a religious or knightly order

explanation.surface: A demanding job set for a prestigious brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a request that is hard to fulfil.

clue.text: Willingness to cook sardines without food additive

indicators.note: without means outside, so the shuffled letters go round the additive
to cook figures is to fiddle them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the prefix of E-numbers, coded food additives

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to prepare sardines with no artificial additives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges SARDINES into READINSS; 'without' means outside, so it goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiness means being prepared and eager, a willingness to act.

clue.text: French dramatist is to keep one company

indicators.note: the outer word holds or keeps the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A playwright's duty is to keep someone company.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Ionesco was a Romanian-born playwright of the Theatre of the Absurd, writing in French.

clue.text: Old dictator received total American backing

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the joined words from back to front

parts.note: all means total, the whole

explanation.surface: A former tyrant enjoyed full support from the Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucius Cornelius Sulla was a Roman general who made himself dictator of Rome.

clue.text: Boss was upset by Turner's rubbish

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised ornamental knob

explanation.surface: The boss was annoyed by the painter Turner's junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' mixes STUD and WAS into SAWDUST. Turner is not the painter but a woodturner, whose lathe produces this waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturner's lathe throws off fine wood shavings and powder as waste.

clue.text: In Charleston I am close to the country

indicators.note: the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone dancing the Charleston feels near to the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The run lies inside 'Charleston I am'; 'close to' only joins the hidden run to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic nation in north-eastern Europe.

clue.text: The lash of the whip

parts.note: the flexible leather strip that forms the striking part of a whip, which also has a modern sense as skimpy underwear

explanation.definitionFit: The narrow leather strap of a whip is its flexible cutting part.

clue.text: A golfer's warning in the past

parts.note: taken as written
golfers shout fore to warn of a ball in flight

explanation.surface: A golfer once called out a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Afore is an archaic or dialect word meaning before, earlier.

clue.text: Where Welsh dockers may unload fresh wine

parts.note: fresh means new
port is a fortified Portuguese wine

explanation.surface: Welsh dockworkers unload a shipment of new wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Newport is a port city in south Wales with large docks.

clue.text: Adjusts the aperture and lies low

definitions.meaning: photographers reduce the lens opening by moving to a higher f-number
to go to ground, keeping out of sight, like a hiding fugitive

explanation.definitionFit: A photographer narrows the lens opening this way, and the phrasal verb also means remain hidden.

clue.text: Subject to getting articles from Europe

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: Someone is controlled by acquiring items from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Under means governed by or liable to, as in under orders.

clue.text: Leave a punter to up the ante

parts.note: go means leave, depart
a punter is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: A gambler is told to raise the stakes before departing.
explanation.definitionFit: To go one better is an idiom for outdoing or raising the stakes on someone.
